quizName: DMV Practice Test #8 20 Questions • Passing Score 16

questions.question: Before changing lanes to the left, what should you do?

options.text: Check your left mirror, then look over your left shoulder.
Check your right mirror, then your left mirror.
Check your left mirror, then your right mirror.
Use your horn, then speed up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your left mirror, then look over your left shoulder.
questions.explanation: Always check the mirror on the side you are moving toward. Also turn your head and look over your shoulder to check your blind spot.

questions.question: With a properly adjusted mirror, what can you see?

options.text: Only the lane beside you.
Only the lane behind you.
The lane behind you and part of the lane next to you.
Everything behind and to the side of your motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: The lane behind you and part of the lane next to you.
questions.explanation: Adjust your mirrors to see the lane behind you and as much as possible of the lane next to you. Properly adjusted mirrors help you stay aware of traffic around you.

questions.question: When entering a curve, a group of riders should ride in what formation?

options.text: Single-file formation.
Staggered formation.
Pairs.
On the shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Single-file formation.
questions.explanation: Use single-file formation when turning, taking curves, or entering or exiting a highway. Staggered formation is best on straight roads.

questions.question: Why should you avoid riding alongside another rider?

options.text: It allows you to use more of the road.
It limits your escape routes.
It makes it easier to communicate.
It makes it easier for other drivers to pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: It limits your escape routes.
questions.explanation: Riding alongside another motorcycle limits your options if you need to escape a hazard.

questions.question: What is engine braking?

options.text: It is illegal.
It is slowing down by turning the engine off.
It is slowing down by downshifting.
It damages the engine.

questions.correctAnswerText: It is slowing down by downshifting.
questions.explanation: Engine braking means shifting to a lower gear to slow down. This produces braking power without using the brakes.

questions.question: When should you wear reflective clothing?

options.text: Never.
Only during the day.
Only at night.
Day and night.

questions.correctAnswerText: Day and night.
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen in daylight. Wearing bright colors and reflective materials at all times helps other drivers see you.

questions.question: Choose a lane position that:

options.text: Reduces your space around you and helps others see you.
Gives you more space around you and helps others see you.
Increases hazards and allows others to pass you.
Reduces hazards and lets you follow vehicles closely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Gives you more space around you and helps others see you.
questions.explanation: Choose a position that increases your space cushion. This helps you see others, be seen, avoid wind blasts and blind spots, and escape hazards.

questions.question: If your motorcycle starts to wobble, what should you do?

options.text: Gradually brake.
Accelerate.
Grip the handlebars firmly and slowly close the throttle.
Downshift.

questions.correctAnswerText: Grip the handlebars firmly and slowly close the throttle.
questions.explanation: Do not speed up, as this makes wobbling worse. Instead, hold the handlebars firmly, close the throttle slowly, move your weight forward and down, and pull off the road. Avoid braking, as this can also worsen the wobble.

questions.question: Riders without helmets are how many times more likely to die in a crash?

options.text: Half as likely
Twice as likely
Three times as likely
Just as likely

questions.correctAnswerText: Three times as likely
questions.explanation: Riders without helmets are three times more likely to die from head injuries in a crash than riders wearing helmets.

questions.question: How much of a motorcycle's braking power does the front brake provide?

options.text: Less than half.
About 70 percent.
It should only be used on wet roads.
It should be the only brake you use.

questions.correctAnswerText: About 70 percent.
questions.explanation: The front brake is much more powerful than the rear brake and provides about 70 percent of total braking power. Use both brakes whenever you slow down or stop.

questions.question: Long periods of riding in cold weather can cause all of the following, except:

options.text: Fatigue.
Hypothermia.
Severe chills.
Hot flashes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hot flashes.
questions.explanation: Cold weather riding can cause severe chills, fatigue, and hypothermia. Wear proper clothing to protect yourself from the cold.

questions.question: What reduces the effects of alcohol after you drink it?

options.text: Exercise
Coffee
Time
Food

questions.correctAnswerText: Time
questions.explanation: Your liver breaks down alcohol at a fixed rate. Nothing can speed up this process. Only time will reduce the effects of alcohol in your body.

questions.question: In a normal turn:

options.text: The motorcycle and rider should lean together.
The motorcycle and rider should lean in opposite directions.
The motorcycle should lean, but the rider should not.
The rider should lean, but the motorcycle should not.

questions.correctAnswerText: The motorcycle and rider should lean together.
questions.explanation: During normal turns, the motorcycle and rider lean together at the same angle. In slow, tight turns, only the motorcycle leans while the rider stays upright.

questions.question: Where is the gear shift lever located?

options.text: In front of the left footrest.
In front of the right footrest.
Behind the left footrest.
Behind the right footrest.

questions.correctAnswerText: In front of the left footrest.
questions.explanation: The gear shift lever is in front of the left footrest. You operate it with your left foot. Lift your foot under the lever to shift up. Press the lever down to shift down.

questions.question: Where is the rear brake control usually located?

options.text: On the right handlebar.
On the left handlebar.
Near the left foot.
Near the right foot.

questions.correctAnswerText: Near the right foot.
questions.explanation: The rear brake is operated by your right foot.

questions.question: How can you reduce your chances of being in a crash?

options.text: Don't use your turn signals when changing lanes.
Follow other vehicles closely.
Watch only five feet ahead of your motorcycle.
Always be ready to use crash-avoidance techniques.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always be ready to use crash-avoidance techniques.
questions.explanation: To reduce crash risk, stay visible to others. Use turn signals, brake lights, and proper lane position. Keep space around your motorcycle. Look ahead, behind, and to the sides. Always be ready to avoid hazards.

questions.question: How do you brake in a straight line with the most stopping power?

options.text: Use only the rear brake.
Use only the front brake.
Use both brakes without locking either wheel.
Use both brakes and lock the rear wheel.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes without locking either wheel.
questions.explanation: On a straight road, use both brakes together to stop in the shortest distance. Avoid locking either brake.

questions.question: Is braking in a turn easier or harder than braking on a straightaway?

options.text: Easier than braking on a straightaway.
More difficult than braking on a straightaway.
Safe when using the front brake only.
Safe when using the rear brake only.

questions.correctAnswerText: More difficult than braking on a straightaway.
questions.explanation: Braking in a turn is harder than braking straight. You can use both brakes in a turn, but you need proper technique and careful control.

questions.question: When riding over rough surfaces, how should you grip the handlebars?

options.text: Hold them loosely to allow for movement.
Hold them firmly to maintain control.
Use lots of throttle to get over the rough surface.
Ride without a helmet so it doesn't cover your face.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold them firmly to maintain control.
questions.explanation: Grip the handlebars firmly when riding over rough surfaces. This keeps you in control of your motorcycle.

questions.question: What is the best way to handle a slippery surface?

options.text: Use the rear brake lightly while crossing.
Slow down before reaching the surface.
Gradually accelerate over the surface.
Downshift when you reach the surface.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down before reaching the surface.
questions.explanation: Reduce your speed before entering a slippery surface. This lowers your risk of skidding.
